target.title: fix(mcp): bound HTTP response body reads at 1 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes an issue where MCP server responses with large bodies could exhaust process memory. The `ensureGlobalFetchResponse` function read `response.text()` without any size check — a misconfigured or malicious MCP server returning hundreds of megabytes would buffer the entire body in memory, risking OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made
Single-chokepoint fix at `ensureGlobalFetchResponse` — both callers in `buildManagedMcpResponse` converge through this function. Two-layer guard:

1. **Content-Length pre-check** — rejects before `response.text()` when the header declares an oversized body (including non-numeric values like `"abc"` which produce `NaN`).
2. **Post-read byte-length guard** — uses `Buffer.byteLength(text, "utf8")` for accurate byte measurement, catching oversized bodies that arrive without a Content-Length header.

Cap is **1 MiB**, matching the merged `CONVEX_BROKER_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` precedent in #98619.

## User Impact
MCP server responses larger than 1 MiB are rejected with a clear error message instead of silently consuming unbounded memory until the process crashes.

## Evidence

**Vitest:** 15/15 passed (10 existing + 5 new tests)
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-http-fetch.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  15 passed (15)
```

**New tests:**
- `rejects body-less responses whose Content-Length exceeds the 1 MiB cap`
- `rejects body-less responses whose actual text exceeds the 1 MiB cap`
- `accepts body-less responses within the 1 MiB cap`
- `accepts responses with Content-Length exactly at the 1 MiB cap` (boundary)
- `rejects responses with non-numeric Content-Length header`
